119a1: The comparisons with one another, as has been said,
119a2: must be made. And the same commonplaces are useful also for proving
119a4: Toward the superiority of another. For if the more honourable is more choiceworthy, and
119a5: the honourable is choiceworthy, and if the more useful is more choiceworthy, and
119a6: the useful is choiceworthy. And likewise also in the case of the others, as many as
119a9: we say, for example when one thing is good by nature and the other not by nature
119a10: let us say; for clearly that which is good by nature is choiceworthy
